words.definition: having a strong wish to succeed or achieve more

sentences.sentence: She’s an ambitious student who wants to study medicine abroad.
His ambitious plan impressed the company directors.
Is this goal too ambitious for our timeline?

words.definition: working well without wasting time or energy

sentences.sentence: The new system is far more efficient than the old one.
She’s an efficient worker who finishes tasks on time.
Is this the most efficient way to share files?

words.definition: upset because you cannot do or change something

sentences.sentence: He felt frustrated because his efforts weren’t recognised.
I get frustrated when people don’t listen carefully.
Are you frustrated with the slow progress?

words.definition: believing that good things will happen

sentences.sentence: He remains optimistic about finding a new job soon.
The doctor was optimistic that she would recover quickly.
Are you optimistic about the outcome?

words.definition: believing that bad things will happen

sentences.sentence: He is too pessimistic and always expects the worst outcome.
Her pessimistic attitude made the whole team lose motivation.
Why are you so pessimistic about the plan?

words.definition: able to do things by yourself; not needing help

sentences.sentence: She became independent after moving to another city.
The company remains independent despite several offers.
Are you independent enough to work alone?

words.definition: worried and nervous about something that may happen

sentences.sentence: She felt anxious before speaking in front of a large audience.
He became anxious waiting for her reply.
Are you anxious about the interview?

words.definition: feeling thanks for help or kindness

sentences.sentence: I’m very grateful for your help during the move.
We’re grateful that nobody was injured in the accident.
Aren’t you grateful for the support?

words.definition: showing strong interest and excitement

sentences.sentence: The students were enthusiastic about the new project.
Her enthusiastic response encouraged the whole team.
Are they enthusiastic about joining?

words.definition: able to change or be changed easily

sentences.sentence: Our schedule is flexible, so we can change the time if needed.
She has a flexible approach to solving problems.
Is this arrangement flexible enough for you?

words.definition: having a strong decision to do something and not giving up

sentences.sentence: He is determined to pass the exam this time.
They were determined to finish before the deadline.
Are you determined to change careers?

words.definition: making you feel uncomfortable; difficult to deal with

sentences.sentence: It was an awkward moment when nobody answered.
There was an awkward silence after his comment.
Does this conversation feel awkward to you?

words.definition: feeling shy and uncomfortable because of a mistake

sentences.sentence: He felt embarrassed when he forgot her name.
She looked embarrassed after making a mistake in class.
Are you embarrassed to ask for help?

words.definition: fair and sensible

sentences.sentence: That’s a reasonable price for such a high-quality product.
It seems reasonable to take a break after two hours.
Is this timeline reasonable for the team?

words.definition: causing admiration because it is very good or large

sentences.sentence: The presentation was impressive, even though it was short.
His knowledge of the subject is really impressive.
Wasn’t her performance impressive?

words.definition: can be trusted to work well or to do what is promised

sentences.sentence: He’s a reliable colleague who always meets deadlines.
The data seems reliable because it comes from official sources.
Is this source reliable?

words.definition: complex and advanced; well designed

sentences.sentence: The software uses a sophisticated algorithm to analyse data.
It’s a sophisticated device that requires careful handling.
Is this solution too sophisticated for beginners?

words.definition: not easily believing; doubting something is true

sentences.sentence: I’m sceptical about the results until I see the evidence.
He was sceptical of the company’s promises.
Are you sceptical about these claims?

words.definition: very surprising and hard to believe; amazing

sentences.sentence: The view from the mountain was absolutely incredible.
It’s incredible how quickly technology changes.
Wasn’t that concert incredible?

words.definition: very important and necessary

sentences.sentence: It’s crucial to check your work before submitting it.
Good communication is crucial for a strong relationship.
Is funding the most crucial issue now?
